episode_title: A Smarter Borrowing Strategy for Entrepreneurs and High Earners with Joseph Wang (Ep. 10)

real_qa.q: How does SyntheticFi's box spread borrowing strategy compare to traditional margin loans in terms of interest rates?
real_qa.r: Box spread borrowing through SyntheticFi offers rates around 4%, whereas traditional margin loans through providers like Schwab typically charge 11-12% based on account values. The lower rates come from the box spread being priced at treasury rates plus a 20-30 basis point spread, determined by the prevailing market cost of capital in the options market, rather than a bank maximizing profits on the loan.
real_qa.requete: SyntheticFi box spread vs margin loan rates

real_qa.q: What is the tax deductibility advantage of using box spreads for borrowing compared to other loan types?
real_qa.r: Box spreads are treated as trades, not loans, so the interest cost is actually a capital loss subject to Section 1256 of the IRS code. This means 60% of the loss can be used as a long-term capital loss deduction and 40% as a short-term capital loss deduction, which can offset $3,000 of ordinary income per year or carry forward indefinitely to offset capital gains, unlike traditional loans which offer no tax deduction.
real_qa.requete: box spread tax deductible IRS Section 1256

real_qa.q: Why did SyntheticFi choose to focus on box spread borrowing instead of pursuing other fintech solutions like AI outreach tools or tax planning software?
real_qa.r: Joseph Wong and his co-founder tested several ideas including RIA AI outreach tools and smart tax planning tools, both of which later became successful companies. However, a conversation with an advisor six months into development—who specifically asked to build the box spread borrowing tool because he had a client who could save significant money using it—provided the clearest validation of demand, prompting them to commit fully to developing the box spread product.
real_qa.requete: SyntheticFi why box spread instead tax planning AI

real_qa.q: How large is the daily trading volume in the box spread and S&P 500 index options markets that SyntheticFi leverages?
real_qa.r: The box spread market clears approximately $2 billion in new borrowings per day, while the entire SPX (S&P 500 index) options market represents a $1 trillion per day market. This massive liquidity ensures that market makers like Citadel, Susquehanna, and Jane Street compete to offer the most efficient borrowing rates, preventing large financial institutions from charging excessive premiums.
real_qa.requete: box spread market volume $2 billion daily SPX options

real_qa.q: What real-world use cases have SyntheticFi clients deployed box spread borrowing for, beyond purchasing lifestyle items?
real_qa.r: SyntheticFi's 250 RIA partners report diverse use cases including buying agricultural properties and revenue-generating facilities (saving one client $60,000 per month in interest payments), financing business acquisitions, implementing buy-borrow-die strategies to minimize cash outflow and preserve assets for heirs with step-up basis, diversifying concentrated stock portfolios, and angel investing in Silicon Valley, demonstrating flexibility across mortgage-like fixed-rate scenarios to short-term line-of-credit situations.
real_qa.requete: SyntheticFi client use cases box spread borrowing farm business

real_qa.q: How does the Options Clearing Corporation's role as counterparty reduce risk and borrowing costs in box spread transactions?
real_qa.r: The Options Clearing Corporation (OCC) guarantees all box spread contracts, meaning borrowers don't face individual bank counterparty risk like they would with Schwab or Bank of America. The OCC has never failed to clear any contracts, even during 2008, and has a higher credit rating than most banks. Because the OCC is essentially 'too big to fail' and simply makes a market rather than maximizing profit margins, borrowing rates reflect only treasuries plus a small spread instead of additional bank markups.
real_qa.requete: Options Clearing Corporation OCC box spread counterparty guarantee

guest.bio_context: Joseph Wong has a background in finance and serving family offices, with experience working with Registered Investment Advisors (RIAs). He traded box spreads for family offices before co-founding SyntheticFi with Tony in 2023, a Y Combinator-backed fintech company that democratized institutional-grade securities-backed lending to independent financial advisors and their clients.
